findings.message: The org and project are read from the clone URL only when it has the form `https://[user@]dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_git/<repo>`. Two other forms of the same Azure DevOps URL fall through silently to the shared secret's org and project. The first is the legacy host `https://<org>.visualstudio.com[/DefaultCollection]/<project>/_git/<repo>`, which `Build.Repository.Uri` still returns for older orgs. The second is any change of case in the host (`Dev.Azure.com`). In both cases the pod quietly uses the wrong project, which is the defect this change exists to fix. The new test pins the wrong result (`https://acme.visualstudio.com/proj/_git/r>o|p`). Fix: also parse the `<org>.visualstudio.com` form (org from the subdomain, with an optional `DefaultCollection/`) and match the host case-insensitively. Add those rows to the `azdo_project_from_url` table.
findings.scenario: FLEET_REPO_URL=https://acme.visualstudio.com/Proj2/_git/r and the fleet-azdo secret has AZDO_PROJECT=Proj1 → the pod exports AZDO_PROJECT=Proj1. draft-pr and the specclaw-azdo-pr/-issue calls then target Proj1, where repo r does not exist, so the PR is never created.

findings.message: The README says the sidecar serves Postgres on `127.0.0.1`. The official postgres image's entrypoint sets `listen_addresses='*'`, so the server also listens on the pod IP, with a known default password. Any pod that can route to this one could reach the test database. Pass `args: [-c, listen_addresses=127.0.0.1]` (the startup probe already uses 127.0.0.1) so the code matches the docs.

`sidecar_before_agent` checks only PGHOST and PGPORT in the agent's env and only the `pgdata` volume. It does not check that the agent gets PGUSER, PGPASSWORD and PGDATABASE, or that the `pgrun` and `pgtmp` volumes the sidecar mounts are declared. Dropping any of them would leave the test green. Assert them all, with non-default user, password and db values so the defaults cannot mask a mix-up.
